To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extracellular protein TSP-1 is modified with O-β-Nacetylglucosaminyl (GlcNAc) on Ser580 of the first EGF-like module, that the modification is catalyzed by a protein that we call OGTSP-1, and that the modification is removed by an N-acetylhexosamine-specific β-1,4-glycosidase.
O-β-GlcNac modification occurs on the fifth and sixth EGF-like modules of TSP1 and TSP2, and that the modification is localized to the serine at position 580 of TSP-2 and TSP-1.

O-β-GlcNac modification occurs on a number of proteins, and the modification is associated with a variety of cellular processes.
TSP-1 is modified by O-fucosyl- and O-β-N- acetylglucosaminyl- glycosylation and by C-mannosyl-glycosylation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
O-β-GlcNac is not restricted to nuclear proteins.
the Notch loop is a conserved motif for modification with O-β-GlcNac, and that the Notch homolog TSP-1 also undergoes this modification.
O-β-GlcNac is a modification that can occur in the extracellular milieu and not just in the cytoplasm.
